This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This petition has been filed seeking quashment of Final Challan No.1/2022 of Crime No.09/2022 dated 21/01/2022 (Annexure P/1) and ensued proceedings of RCT No.355/2022 pending in the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur.
2.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is contended by the counsel that on 07/01/2022 respondent No.2/complainant who is wife of applicant No.1 Nirendra Kumar Dubey, lodged FIR with Mahila Thana Jabalpur wherein,
allegations of demand of dowry and cruelty were levelled.
It is contended by the counsel that in the complaint, all relatives of the applicant No.1, have been implicated without even disclosing the fact that they are not even residing in common household.
It is also contended by the counsel that there are omnibus and general allegations against the applicants, therefore, the FIR and ensued proceedings deserve to be set aside.

3. It is also contended by the counsel that the FIR reflects that respondent No.2/complainant was keeping grudge as according to respondent No.2, after marriage of her brother-in-law (Devar),
importance was being given to the wife of brother-in-law (Devar), therefore, the complainant felt offended which persuaded her to lodge the FIR.

Learned counsel contends that there are no specific allegations the applicants and after nine years of marriage, FIR has been lodged despite the fact that applicant No.1 and respondent No.2 are parents of two children.

To support his contentions learned counsel has placed reliance in the cases of Preeti Gupta and another v. State of Jharkhand and another reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667 and Geeta Mehrotra and another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741, therefore, prays that the entire proceedings deserves to be quashed.
4.

entities.text: Preeti Gupta and another v. State of Jharkhand and another reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra and another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents have opposed the prayer and it is contended by the counsel for the respondents that the statement of the complainant reveals that specific allegations have been levelled against the present applicants and there are allegations of demand of dowry.

It is also contended by the counsel that it is difficult for complainant to remember the Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137892612/
2 specific date on which she was subjected to cruelty inasmuch as, during a prolong period of almost 9 years form the date of marriage, on various occasions, respondent No.2/complainant was subjected to cruelty.

entities.text: Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the present petition deserves to be dismissed.
5. No other point is pressed or argued by the parties.

6. Heard rival submissions of the parties and perused the record.
7.
As per the allegations levelled in the FIR, the respondent No.2 subjected to cruelty and demanded dowry.
As per the FIR at the time of marriage, on being demanded by the present applicants, apart form Rs.3,00,000/- cash, other household items were given to the applicants.

After marriage,
according to complainant, she was subjected to torture and cruelty by the present applicants and dowry was being demanded.
The respondent No.2 was ill treated, manhandled and abused.

The FIR futher reflects that there are allegations against the applicant No.4 Neeraj Dubey (Devar of respondent No.2) that he had stolen ornaments of respondent No.2 but in order to save marriage,
no action was taken by the respondent No.2.

Thereafter, marriage of applicant No.4-Neeraj Dubey (Devar) was solemnized with applicant No.5-Pinki Dubey who is sister-in-law (Devrani of respondent No.2) and as she had brought dowry from her parents house, she was given importance and respondent No.2 was again subjected to cruelty and there was further demand of Rs.3,00,000/-
as dowry by the present applicants.

It is further mentioned that on 01/04/2020 when the father of respondent No.2 visited the house of the applicants and requested them to allow respondent No.2 to live in the house, he was also ill treated and dowry was demanded by the applicants.
8.

A perusal of FIR reflects that there are omnibus allegations against the applicant No.2-Lakhan Dubey, applicant No.3-Smt. Devaki Dubey and applicant No.5-Pinki Dubey as according to FIR itself the individual overt act on the part of applicant No.2 & 3 have not been detailed in the FIR.
Simultaneously, the applicant No.5 was later married to complainant's Devar (applicant No.4).
There are no specific allegations against the applicant No.5 also.
It is being alleged by levelling omnibus allegation that applicant No.5 also along with other applicants, demanded dowry.

The Apex Court has considered the aspect of implication of relatives/family members of the husband in matrimonial cases and while dealing with the other cases recently, the the Apex Court in the case of Kahakashan Kausar alias Sonam and others v. State of Bihar and others [(2022) 6SCC 599] in paragraphs 16 and 18 has held as under:
"16. Recently, in K. Subba Rao v. State of Telangana [K. Subba Rao v. State of Telangana, (2018) 14 SCC 452 :
(2019) 1 SCC (Cri) 605] , it was also observed that :
(SCC p. 454, para 6) "6. ... The courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: Kahakashan Kausar alias Sonam and others v. State of Bihar and others [(2022) 6SCC 599]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
K. Subba Rao v. State of Telangana [K. Subba Rao v. State of Telangana, (2018) 14 SCC 452 :
(2019) 1 SCC (Cri) 605]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out."
Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137892612/
3 18.

entities.text: Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 1-4-2019, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the appellants.
The complainant alleged that "all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy".

Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the appellants herein i.e. none of the appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.

The allegations are, therefore,
general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High Court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution."
9. In the cases of prosecution of the relatives/family members of husband, the allegations are required to be evaluated carefully, and even reading between the line is also imperative.

The instances of ignorable fracas and conflict, usually result in launching of prosecution of the husband and while launching the prosecution of the husband, if the relatives are being also implicated, in such an eventuality, it becomes necessary to evaluate few necessary circumstances like whether the prosecutrix was actually residing with the family members/relatives who have been implicated.
If the prosecutrix was residing in a common house hold then what was the exact specific overt act on the part of the each family member/relative.
The prosecutrix is further required to level specific allegations against each relative if she has been subjected to cruelty by them.

Furthermore, if the relatives/family members are not residing with the prosecutrix, than the prosecutrix is required to specify as to whether she was subjected to cruelty indirectly by any other communication like phone or messages etc.

10 In the case of Abhishek v. State of Madhya Pradesh [2023 LiveLaw(SC) 731] the Apex Court in paragraph 13 and 16 has held as under:
1 3 . Instances of a husband's family members filing a petition to quash criminal proceedings launched against them by his wife in the midst of matrimonial disputes are neither a rarity nor of recent origin.

entities.text: Abhishek v. State of Madhya Pradesh [2023 LiveLaw(SC) 731]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Precedents aplenty abound on this score.
We may now take note of some decisions of particular relevance.

Recently, in Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others vs. State of Bihar and others [(2022) 6 SCC 599], this Court had occasion to deal with a similar situation where the High Court had refused to quash a FIR registered for various offences, including Section 498A IPC.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others vs. State of Bihar and others [(2022) 6 SCC 599]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Noting that the foremost issue that required determination was whether allegations made against the in-laws were general omnibus allegations which would be liable to be quashed, this Court referred to earlier decisions wherein concern was expressed over the misuse of Section 498A IPC and the increased tendency to implicate relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes.
This Court observed that false implications by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial disputes, if left unchecked, would result in misuse of the process of law.

On the facts of that case, it was found that no specific allegations were made against the in-laws by the wife and it was held that allowing their prosecution in the absence of clear allegations against Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137892612/
4 the in-laws would result in an abuse of the process of law.

entities.text: Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also noted that a criminal trial, leading to an eventual acquittal, would inflict severe scars upon the accused and such an exercise ought to be discouraged.

16. Of more recent origin is the decision of this Court in Mahmood Ali and others vs.
State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 2341 of 2023, decided on 08.08.2023)
on the legal principles applicable apropos Section 482 Cr.P.C. Therein, it was observed that when an accused comes before the High Court, invoking either the inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. or the extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, to get the FIR or the criminal proceedings q u a s h e d , essentially on the ground that such proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive of wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances, the High Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely.

entities.text:
Mahmood Ali and others vs.
State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 2341 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was further observed that it will not be enough for the Court to look into the averments made in the FIR/complaint alone for the purpose of ascertaining whether the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence are disclosed or not as, in frivolous or vexatious proceedings, the Court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above the averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection, to try and read between the lines.
11.

The FIR if scrutinize while keeping in view the law enunciated by the Apex Court in the cases of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam (Supra) and Abhishek (Supra), the same would reveal that there are omnibus, general allegations against applicant Nos.2,3 and 5.
Therefore, the FIR and ensued proceedings so far as they relate to applicant Nos.2,3 & 5 stand quashed and the petition stands allowed.
The bail bonds, if any, stands discharged.

12. As there are specific allegations against applicant Nos.1 & 4, this Court is not inclined to entertain the present petition so far as they relate to applicant Nos.1 & 4.
13.

Thus, this petition stands dismissed as far as the same relates to applicant Nos.1 & 4.
14.
Accordingly, this petition stands partly allowed.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE Astha Nirendra Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137892612/
